entries.title: Psalms 22:1
segments:
This psalm has its chief fulfilment in Christ.  It is fulfilled in all his followers, so far as they constitute his body and suffer with him. 
 
  My God, my God; the language of Christ on the cross.
We should never forget that all the sufferings of the Saviour were for our sakes, that we might be saved from the pangs of the second death, and inherit everlasting life and glory.

entries.title: Psalms 22:2
segments: Thou hearest not; God did not answer in the removal of David's sufferings.

entries.title: Psalms 22:6
segments: I am a worm; exceedingly weak and despised, and treated with contempt.

entries.title: Psalms 22:7
segments: They shoot out the lip; expressive of the manner in which the multitude treated the Saviour.

entries.title: Psalms 22:8
segments:
Let him deliver him; the ironical language of his opposers. 
 
  Seeing he delighted in him; seeing God delighted in this sufferer, who is the Messiah. 
 
The exactness with which the circumstances of our Saviour's crucifixion were foretold more than a thousand years before it took place, is evidence that the Bible inspired, and that holy men in preparing it wrote as they were moved by the Holy Ghost; so that what they wrote is the testimony of God.

entries.title: Psalms 22:9
segments: Thou art he; the language of the Saviour, expressive of his holy confidence in God the Father.

entries.title: Psalms 22:12
segments:
Many bulls; his numerous, fierce, and strong enemies. 
 
  Bulls of Bashan; the fiercest and strongest.

entries.title: Psalms 22:14
segments: Poured out like water; expressive of extreme weakness, the most exhausting sufferings.

entries.title: Psalms 22:16
segments: They pierced my hands and my feet;
The wicked, in crucifying the Lord of glory, did, without intending it or thinking of it, precisely what God declared a thousand years before that they would do.

entries.title: Psalms 22:20
segments: My darling; an expression for his soul or life, as his most precious possession, and one that could not be replaced when destroyed.

entries.title: Psalms 22:21
segments: The horns of the unicorns; the power and malice of his mightiest and most cruel opposers.

entries.title: Psalms 22:22
segments: My brethren; the redeemed, whom Christ made his brethren by taking upon himself their nature.

The victory over his enemies, which the Saviour here anticipates, is shared by all his followers. 
 
The Scriptures were fulfilled not only in the curcifixion of our Lord, but also in his resurrection and the events which followed.

entries.title: Psalms 22:25
segments: I will pay my vows; the vows made in the time of my trouble. According to Hebrew usage, they consisted of thank-offerings, which were a form of peace-offering, and were paid publicly at the tabernacle or temple in the presence of the congregation.
After certain prescribed portions had been burned on the altar, the offerer and his friends feasted on the remainder.
When, on occasions of great joy, kings offered peace-offerings, they made a feast for the whole people.

In allusion to these sacrificial vows of the ancient Hebrews, the mighty sufferer of this psalm, who is David in the type but Christ in the antitype, promises, when he has obtained deliverance, to spread a feast for "all the kindreds of the nations,"
.  Compare

entries.title: Psalms 22:26
segments: Shall eat; of the feast provided by the Redeemer, when he pays his vows for deliverance.  The allusion is to the sacrificial vows of the ancient Hebrews.

entries.title: Psalms 22:27
segments: All the ends of the world; people of all countries.  This shall be the fruit of the Saviour's sufferings.

entries.title: Psalms 22:28
segments: He is the governor among the nations; the rightful King of all people.

entries.title: Psalms 22:29
segments:
All they that be fat upon earth; the rich, great, and powerful. 
 
  They that go down to the dust; the poor, afflicted, and despised. All classes must partake of his salvation, or perish. 
 
The Scriptures will yet be fulfilled in the universal spread of the gospel, and in all people's bowing in cheerful and willing obedience to the Saviour; owning him as the Lord their righteousness and salvation, and giving united, hearty, and everlasting thanks to his great and holy name.

entries.title: Psalms 22:30
segments: A generation; a posterity that shall serve the Lord.

entries.title: Psalms 22:31
segments: Declare his righteousness; they shall declare to those who come after them the righteousness of the Lord as the ground of human hope, and what he has done for the lost children of men.
